# Goal

In this work, students are expected to perform:

- **research** on a topic in the field of Artificial Intelligence applied to Games;
- a **public oral presentation** about the attributed topic, supported by slides and, if appropriate, notes (see [Grades](#grades)).

Optionally, groups may also build a **small Unreal Engine demo** of the technique they researched (see [Optional bonus](#bonus)).

# Topics

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Pathfinding and movement**

1. Search algorithms (A\*, Dijkstra, etc.)
2. Navigation meshes
3. Steering behaviors
4. Swarm intelligence

**Decision making**

5. Finite state machines
6. Behavior Trees
7. Utility AI
8. Goal Oriented Action Planning (GOAP)
9. STRIPS
10. Hierarchical Task Network (HTN) planning

**Tactics and adversarial search**

11. Influence maps
12. Minimax and alpha-beta pruning
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
13. Monte Carlo Tree Search
14. Imperfect-information games (Poker, CFR, Libratus/Pluribus)

**Learning and probabilistic models**

15. Bayesian networks
16. Evolutionary algorithms
17. Recurrent neural networks and LSTM
18. Reinforcement learning in games
19. LLM-driven NPCs

**Emergence and procedural generation**

20. Artificial life
21. Cellular automata
22. Wave Function Collapse

**Other**

23. Student proposal
:::
:::

# Instructions

## Groups and topic choice

- The work should be done in **groups of two students**.
- Each group should choose **three topics in descending order of preference** and **email the list** of chosen topics to your class professor: [gustavo.reis@ulo.pt](mailto:gustavo.reis@ulo.pt) or [luis.m.monteiro@ulo.pt](mailto:luis.m.monteiro@ulo.pt).

  ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
  ## Example
  1. 3 – Steering behaviors *(preferred)*
  2. 2 – Navigation meshes
  3. 14 – Imperfect-information games *(third preference)*
  :::

- The **subject** of the email must start with `[AIAG Research Project]` - we have a filter on our email highlighting  all emails that start with this subject.
- The email must include the identification of the students in the group (**student number and full name**).
- If choosing **Student proposal**, the students must first send an email with the proposed topic so it can be approved.

## Topic attribution

Topics are attributed in the **order in which the emails are received**. Each group gets its highest-ranked topic that is still available. If none of the group's three topics is still available, the group will be contacted to choose another one.

## Both students present

Both group members must present, each for roughly half of the time. Slides are graded per group. Presentation criteria are graded **individually**, so the two students may get different final grades.

## Use of generative AI

Generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) may be used to **search for sources, brainstorm and improve the language** of the slides, under the following conditions:

- Their use must be **disclosed** on the last slide (tool used and what it was used for).
- Every fact and reference must be **verified** against the original source. Fabricated or unverifiable references are penalized in the *References* criterion.
- Students must be able to **explain everything** in their slides during the Q&A.

Undisclosed use of generative AI to produce the content is treated as academic misconduct.

## References

- At least **5 references**, of which at least **3 peer-reviewed** (journal articles, conference papers or academic books).
- Use the **IEEE citation style**, with in-text citations ([1], [2], …) and a final *References* slide.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Finding good sources
To find articles that give a general perspective on a topic, use expressions such as **Overview**, **Survey** or **State of the Art** together with the topic in search engines (e.g. Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library). For didactic introductions to a theme, use, for example, **Tutorial**.
:::

## Submission

All groups must submit the slides through **Moodle by the deadline in [Dates and deadlines](#dates)**, before the first presentation day, regardless of their presentation slot. The file name must follow the format below, where `#1` and `#2` are the student numbers of the group members:

```
AI_research_work_#1_#2.pdf
```

# Grades {#grades}

| Component | Criterion | Weight | Weight (English) ^3^ |
|---|---|:-:|:-:|
| **Slides and notes** ^1^ *(per group)* | Content | 45% | 45% |
| | Organization | 15% | 15% |
| | References | 10% | 10% |
| **Presentation** *(individual)* | Time ^2^ | 7.5% | 5% |
| | Posture, gestures, movements | 7.5% | 5% |
| | Speech | 15% | 10% |
| | English | — | 10% |
| | **Total** | **100%** | **100%** |

1. Slides should be designed so that reading them is enough to give readers a general understanding of the subject, even without seeing the presentation. If slides are designed only as a presentation medium (e.g. image-based slides), they must be accompanied by notes that allow a general understanding of the topic.
2. Presentations must take **10 minutes (±1 minute)**, followed by up to **5 minutes of Q&A**. Presentations are stopped at 12 minutes. The *Time* criterion is graded on how close the presentation is to 10 minutes. Q&A is not graded separately; answers count towards *Speech*.
3. If both the slides and the presentation are in English, the presentation criteria change: 10% is attributed immediately for English, and the remaining presentation criteria are lowered as shown.

## Optional bonus {#bonus}

Groups may present a **short Unreal Engine demo** (≤ 2 minutes, within the 10 minutes) showing the researched technique in action. A working, well-explained demo adds **up to 1 point** (on the 0–20 scale) to the final grade of this work, capped at 20.
